subject: economics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The reward (factor payment) earned by labour is:
questions.explain: Labour earns wages, land earns rent, capital earns interest and enterprise earns profit.

questions.q: In a free market economy, resources are mainly allocated by:
questions.explain: In a market economy the price mechanism allocates resources with no central direction.

questions.q: An outward shift of the whole production possibility curve usually represents:
options: Economic growth from more or better resources
questions.explain: More or improved resources, or better technology, shift the entire PPC outward, showing growth.

questions.q: Capital goods differ from consumer goods because capital goods are:
options: Used to produce other goods and services
Bought by households for final use
questions.explain: Capital goods, like machinery, are used to make other goods rather than for direct consumption.

questions.q: Incentives matter in economics because they:
options: Remove the need to make choices
Influence the decisions of consumers, workers and producers
questions.explain: Incentives such as prices, wages and profits shape how people and firms behave.

questions.q: A movement ALONG a production possibility curve, producing more of good A and less of good B, shows:
options: The opportunity cost of producing more of good A
questions.explain: Reallocating resources to good A means giving up some of good B, illustrating opportunity cost.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'need' rather than a 'want'?
questions.explain: Needs are essential for survival, such as water; wants are desires that improve living standards.

questions.q: Because resources are scarce, every economy must answer the question of:
options: What, how and for whom to produce
questions.explain: Scarcity forces every economy to decide what to produce, how to produce it and for whom.

questions.q: Trade-offs exist because:
options: Choosing more of one thing means giving up some of another due to scarcity
questions.explain: Scarcity means resources used for one purpose cannot be used for another, creating trade-offs.

questions.q: Specialisation and the division of labour are likely to:
options: Guarantee that work is never boring
Make workers skilled at many tasks at once
questions.explain: Dividing tasks lets workers become more efficient at them, raising productivity and total output.

questions.q: What is the basic economic problem?
options: Resources are scarce but human wants are unlimited
Some countries are richer than others
There is too much money in circulation
questions.explain: The economic problem is that scarce resources cannot satisfy unlimited wants, forcing choices.

questions.q: 'Land' as a factor of production includes:
options: Natural resources such as forests, oil and fishing grounds
questions.explain: Land covers all natural resources used in production, including raw materials and gifts of nature.

questions.q: Which of these is a factor of production?
questions.explain: The four factors of production are land, labour, capital and enterprise; money is not one of them.

questions.q: One disadvantage of the division of labour for workers is that:
options: Repetitive tasks can become boring, lowering motivation
questions.explain: Doing the same narrow task repeatedly can be monotonous, reducing worker motivation.

questions.q: Opportunity cost is best defined as:
options: The tax added to a product
The total cost of producing a good
The next best alternative given up when a choice is made
The money price paid for a good
questions.explain: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone when a decision is made.

questions.q: Which best describes 'capital' as a factor of production?
options: Man-made goods used to produce other goods, such as machinery
questions.explain: Capital refers to man-made aids to production such as machines, tools and factories, not money.

questions.q: In a centrally planned economy, the main decision-maker is:
questions.explain: In a command economy the government decides what, how and for whom to produce.

questions.q: Specialisation between countries means each country:
options: Concentrates on what it produces relatively well and trades for the rest
Produces only one single product worldwide
questions.explain: Countries specialise in goods they produce relatively efficiently and trade for others, raising total output.

questions.q: 'Enterprise' as a factor of production refers to:
options: The land a business is built on
The willingness to take risks and combine the other factors
questions.explain: Enterprise is the entrepreneur's role in organising the other factors and bearing risk.

questions.q: A point inside (below) a production possibility curve indicates:
questions.explain: Points inside the PPC show resources are not being fully or efficiently used.

questions.q: Choosing to spend an hour studying instead of working a paid shift means the opportunity cost is:
options: The wages that could have been earned in that hour
The grade achieved in the exam
questions.explain: The opportunity cost of studying is the next best alternative given up, here the wages forgone.

questions.q: A 'mixed economy' is one in which:
options: Resources are allocated by both the market and the government
There is no government at all
questions.explain: A mixed economy combines a private market sector with government provision and regulation.
